I am very concerned about efforts to weaponize artificial intelligence to intimidate and misinform voters.

@RepShontelBrown and I sent a letter to DOJ, DHS, and EAC requesting information about how these agencies plan to secure our election against AI-generated misinformation. https://t.co/ETvtgxTE9k

Generations of Americans, including many in Alabama's 7th Congressional District, fought to ensure that every eligible voter can cast their ballot in free and fair elections. We cannot allow bad actors to weaponize powerful AI tools to mislead voters, suppress turnout, and sow chaos. With only eight months until November, the time is now for our federal agencies to protect Americans against such threats, especially Black voters who have been disproportionately targeted by election mis-information and dis-information.

Today, I'm announcing that I have cosponsored the AI Data Center Moratorium Act.

Alabamians are asking important questions about how the rapid expansion of data centers will impact our water, our environment, and our quality of life. I don't believe we have received sufficient answers, and it's clear that these facilities are being built faster than we can establish the safeguards our communities deserve.

Our bill would pause the construction of these large, AI data centers until Congress can put in place protections for our people, our environment, and the natural resources we all share.

All across Alabama, ordinary people are speaking up because they care about the future of their communities. They deserve to be heard.

Artificial intelligence has the potential to revolutionize health care, strengthen our economy, improve education, and solve some of our nation's greatest challenges. I want America to lead the world in AI innovation, and I want Alabama to compete for the industries of the future. But innovation cannot come at the expense of the communities it is meant to serve.

I am not anti-AI, and I am certainly not anti-innovation. The rate at which these massive data centers are being constructed is simply outpacing our ability to establish meaningful protections for the communities that will host them. Congress has a responsibility to put commonsense federal guardrails in place so that every community—not just a select few—shares in the benefits of this technological revolution.

For too long, underserved communities have been asked to shoulder disproportionate environmental and economic burdens while others reap the rewards. As we build the economy of tomorrow, we must ensure that innovation lifts up every community rather than leaving some to bear the costs. Responsible innovation and community protection are not competing goals—they are complementary ones.

Too often, low-income Black and minority communities have been expected to shoulder the environmental and economic risks of major industrial projects while others reap the rewards. We cannot allow the AI economy to perpetuate this cycle of injustice.

For all these reasons, I recently proposed the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, legislation that would temporarily pause the construction and expansion of AI data centers until Congress establishes comprehensive safeguards addressing environmental, economic, labor, privacy, and community impacts. The goal is not to stop innovation but to ensure that public policy keeps pace with technological change and everyday people collectively share in the benefits of our new future.

Data centers should NOT be getting massive tax breaks, especially when they are building in underserved communities!

This is why I support the AI Data Center Moratorium Act to temporarily stop the construction of new data centers until safeguards are put in place to protect our communities. https://t.co/EIbV1DPvy2
